findings.title: The wave as canopy; the call as purified allegiance
findings.claim: The turbulent wave becomes more than open-water motion: ghashiya physically covers them, and the canopy simile makes the enclosure overhead. Under that pressure, mukhlisin can carry both the removal of admixture from din and the dedication of worship and obedience to Allah alone. The wider layered-wave image in 24:40 and the repeated exclusive-call sequence in 29:65 make this a recurring sea-crisis pattern.
findings.mechanism: The wave noun supplies moving turbulence, the ghashiya verb supplies physical cover, and al-zulal supplies the overhead canopy image; 24:40 independently places waves above waves and darkness above darkness. In the same focus, mukhlisin acts on din for Him, while 98:5 and 40:65 explicitly join worship or calling Allah with religion made exclusive to Him. The contact changes the reading from a large storm alone to outer enclosure answered by an inwardly cleared and exclusively directed allegiance.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene lets the reader feel how a loss of outward horizon can coincide with a clarified act of worship, not just a frightened cry.
findings.containment: The waves and their cover remain literal. The comparison does not claim that danger creates belief or makes the call permanent; 29:65 itself shows renewed association after landfall, and the ordinary senses of calling, religion, and rescue remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and trusted candidate support ground the reading; supplied external parallels activate the wider relation, while the movement from physical cover to inward purification remains interpretive.

findings.title: Landfall as open ground and a test of fidelity
findings.claim: The rescue separates the travelers from the sea and brings them to literal land; that landing can also be an open field on which the crisis-call's truth is tested. The repeated 29:65 rescue-to-land phrase is followed by renewed association, so reaching shore is a change of danger, not a guarantee of enduring allegiance.
findings.mechanism: The focus Form II rescue carries deliverance by separation, and al-barr names the sea's opposite shore. The wider parallel repeats the rescue-to-land sequence but continues with association; contact between the physical endpoint and the post-landing response makes landfall a place where fidelity can become visible.
findings.reader_payoff: Safety is no longer mistaken for the conclusion of the moral sequence: what follows on land shows whether the crisis response holds.
findings.containment: Land remains a concrete shore, and the integrity reading is an added contextual resonance rather than a replacement gloss. The parallel does not imply that every rescued person fails, since the focus itself marks a measured subgroup.

epistemic.reason: The rescue and shore branches are directly supported by the focus and trusted candidate evidence; the ethical test is a contextual inference from the exact 29:65 continuation.

findings.title: A measured course can preserve direction
findings.claim: After rescue, muqtasid can carry both a straight-course sense and a measured middle-course sense: the survivor may retain a sustainable direction when crisis intensity recedes, while a reading of reduced commitment remains live. Wider uses of qasd as a path and muqtasid within a graded community illuminate both readings without deciding between them.
findings.mechanism: The focus places muqtasid after rescue and marks the person as one from among the rescued. In 16:9, qasd names the path while some paths veer; 31:19 applies qasd to walking; 35:32 uses muqtasid for one profile among graded responses. These independent contexts make course and measure available through the focus word without collapsing them.
findings.reader_payoff: The word need not label either lukewarmness or complete constancy: it can show a survivor maintaining a measured bearing, with the amount of fidelity still open.
findings.containment: The comparison does not decide whether muqtasid here means straightness or moderation, equate the different communities, or erase the possibility of diminished commitment. The short-journey branch is excluded.

epistemic.reason: The focus form and trusted candidate support ground both nominated qasd branches; the external contexts expand them but do not disambiguate the focus.

findings.title: Knowing denial as betrayal after rescue
findings.claim: The closing clause pairs denial of divine signs with the profile of a habitual trust-breaker and ingrate. Since the focus places that refusal after rescue, the denial can be read as a breach of experienced favor and relationship, alongside the coexisting sense of rejecting religious truth. Wider sea-to-landfall scenes repeat turning away or renewed association after rescue.
findings.mechanism: Yajhadu is attached to Our signs, khattar names betrayal of trust, and kafur names intensive ingratitude. The focus sequence supplies rescue before that profile; 17:67 repeats rescue to land and calls the turn-away ungrateful, while 29:65 ends the same rescue-to-land formula with association. The 29:49 signs passage clarifies the denial as directed at manifest signs, and 22:38 pairs treachery with ingratitude.
findings.reader_payoff: The final warning becomes a diagnosis of knowing relational failure after a received benefit, rather than a description of someone who merely lacked evidence.
findings.containment: The focus does not explicitly say that rescue itself is one of the signs, so that link remains an inference from sequence and parallel. The familiar ingratitude reading remains intact; the doctrinal-denial and relationship-severance branches coexist, and the focus's measured subgroup is not erased.

epistemic.reason: The focus words and trusted candidate support directly ground signs, knowing denial, betrayal, and ingratitude; the move from rescue to experienced relational obligation is contextual.

findings.title: Two separations, inward and outward
findings.claim: The focus places an inward clearing of religious allegiance beside an outward rescue that removes the travelers from the sea. The exact 29:65 parallel repeats exclusive devotion and rescue to land, then turns to association, so the two separations can mirror one another without promising that either endures.
findings.mechanism: Mukhlisin carries purification of din, while the rescue-and-land phrase describes physical extraction from danger. Their distinct carriers meet through the crisis sequence, and 29:65 repeats the same outer and devotional sequence before showing that landfall can be followed by renewed association.
findings.reader_payoff: The rescue can be seen at two scales: an inward clearing of allegiance and a bodily exit from danger, with the external parallel keeping the inner state from becoming an automatic guarantee.
findings.containment: The mirror is an interpretive analogy, not a dictionary equivalence between purification and rescue. The outside verse repeats the sequence but does not say that rescue causes sincerity.

epistemic.reason: The candidate's own support marks the mirror as an inference; exact 29:65 text independently anchors the repeated outer sequence, while the inward-outward correspondence remains analogical.

findings.title: The sea-call within a field of competing summons
findings.claim: Across 31:21 and 31:30, people are pressed by competing calls: inherited practice is chosen over what was revealed, Satan calls toward punishment, and what is called besides Allah is named false. Against that wider field, the focus's exclusive call under the wave is a temporary alignment of caller, addressee, and destination; landfall leaves its continuation open.
findings.mechanism: The focus daʿaw occurrence carries calling toward an addressee, and mukhlisin makes din exclusive for Allah. The exact context traces provide rival calls in 31:21 and a true/false contrast in 31:30; these independent relations return through the focus call and exclusive-din phrase, changing an isolated plea into a reorientation within competing summons.
findings.reader_payoff: The crisis narrows a wider contest of direction to one addressee, while the post-rescue clause asks what survives after the pressure lifts.
findings.containment: The wider call pattern does not prove that relapse is caused by another caller, and the focus does not explain every motive for post-rescue conduct. The competition is a contextual reading, not a replacement for the literal plea.

epistemic.reason: The supplied exact Arabic and HFT occurrence coordinates support each context contact, but their roots, indices, and assigned roles remain attributed and the reorientation is inferential.

findings.mechanism: The repeated outside sequence supplies a recurring relapse trigger; the focus returns through the partitive phrase, the qasd person-label, and the restrictive closing clause. Their contact changes the landfall from a single outcome into a visible distribution of post-crisis responses, with measured continuity for some and denial for the described ingrate.

findings.containment: The outside passages are parallels, not a statistical claim that every rescued person relapses. The focus does not say its two profiles exhaust every outcome, and the readings are not ranked.

epistemic.reason: The focus partitive and qasd wording is directly supplied and the two external sequences have exact Arabic; the synthesis of them as a recurring pattern is interpretive.
